To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
distal CpG islands upstream of genes with methyl-silenced proximal promoters function as alternative promoters in a tissue-dependent fashion.

a large fraction of human genes with methylated promoters are transcribed by an unmethylated distal upstream CpGI, and the transcripts initiated from the distal CpGI are associated with signals indicative of stable elongation, splicing, and expression.

a sizable number of human genes are expressed in a tissue-specific manner when the neighboring distal CpG island (located several kilobases upstream) is unmethylated, and that such genes exhibit signals of stable elongating transcription and splicing that start at the distal CpG islands and extend into the gene bodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional role of DNA methylation at proximally located CGIs in regulating tissue-specific expression patterns of human genes.
the identification, characterization and functional significance of alternative promoters, and the mechanisms underlying the regulation of gene expression in a tissue-specific manner.
the role of DNA methylation in transcriptional control of mammalian genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
distal CpG islands are a major source of alternative transcription start sites in human cells.
distal CpG islands are alternative promoters of genes with methylating proximal promoters, and the expression is regulated by DNA methylation of these distal CGIs.
a sizable fraction of methylated proximal gene promoters are not transcriptionally silent and are transcribed by a distal CpG island that functions as an alternate promoter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a substantial fraction of tissue-specific gene expression in humans can be explained by the activity of distal CpG islands that function as alternative promoters.
a substantial proportion of genes with silenced promoters are transcribed by an alternative promoter located upstream, which is active only when unmethylated.
a sizable number of genes with methyl-silenced proximal promoters are actually transcribed from an alternative upstream promoter, and that such genes are under greater evolutionary constraints.
The main takeaway from our work is that
distal CGIs can function as alternative promoters and can be a source of tissue-specific expression.
DNA methylation at a gene promoter does not necessarily imply its transcriptional silencing.
DNA methylation at a promoter does not necessarily silence gene expression.
